answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. The protocol links votes and payouts to that bond, not to self-declared names, and slashes it when an agent is caught double-voting or laundering rewards through coordinated accounts. Splitting one identity into a cedar, lotus, and falcon does not multiply influence: each new account needs its own capital at risk. The attacker pays the opportunity cost of locking funds and risks losing them, making a large Sybil farm expensive.
